Our Story: Past, Present & Future
Discover the story of Reigate Grammar School: from our historic 1675 foundation to a thriving, forward-looking school community focused on excellence and growth.
About RGS
Our History
A Tradition of Happy Kids and Great Results!
The Grammar School tradition that has shaped RGS continues to underpin our approach today, but with a distinctly modern ethos. At the heart of everything we do is a simple belief: happy kids get great results. Academic success remains a key aim, but it is never pursued in isolation. We foster aspiration, discipline and a deep sense of personal growth, while ensuring our pupils feel supported, confident and joyful in their learning.
Guided by a passionate and dedicated teaching staff, our students are prepared for entry to leading universities and for life beyond, nurtured in an environment that values their moral, social and cultural development just as highly as their grades.
GCSE Grades 7 – 9 in 2024
of A Level grades were A*
Of all grades were 9
Of students achieved at least five grade 4s (A-C equivalent)*
Were grade 7-9 across all subjects
Our Foundations
The first foundation of Reigate Grammar School is recorded in 1675, when Henry Smith, an alderman of London, bequeathed £150 towards the purchase of land for a “free school.” The remainder of the money was raised locally, and in 1684 the vicar of Reigate, the Rev. John Williamson, was appointed Master.
At that time, the school was very small – records suggest just “four poor boys” were enrolled, though others likely attended on a fee-paying basis and boarded with the Master.
Historic Roots
For many years, the school remained closely linked to the parish church of St Mary’s, with successive Headmasters also serving as vicars. In 1862, RGS was re-formed as a grammar school with a board of governors, new buildings, and a growing pupil roll – rising from 36 pupils to a significantly larger cohort in the years that followed.
Under the Education Act of 1944, the school came under Surrey County Council’s control before reverting to independent status in 1976. Girls were first admitted to the Sixth Form in 1976, and to the whole school in 1993.
Though RGS is non-denominational today and welcomes pupils of all faiths and none, our Christian heritage and our connection to St Mary’s Church remain valued aspects of school life, with traditional Christian assemblies continuing to take place there.
A Growing Family of Schools
Our community has grown in recent years through a series of strategic partnerships:
Each of these schools shares the RGS ethos and high standards, while continuing to flourish as a distinctive school in its own right — with a unique personality, strong parent community, and individual strengths. As part of the wider RGS family, they also benefit from the collective expertise and support of a successful, values-driven group, creating lasting opportunities for every pupil.
The Andy Paul Sport and Activity Centre
We are now looking ahead to our most ambitious development to date:
The Andy Paul Sport and Activity Centre, due to open in 2027.
Thanks to a generous gift from former pupil Andy Paul, and the support of our RGS International partnerships, this cutting-edge facility will include:
Construction begins in April 2026. This project builds on the success of the Harrison Centre and reflects our ongoing commitment to wellbeing, excellence, and future generations of RGS students.
A competition-standard Sports Hall
A fitness and conditioning suite
A dance and multipurpose studio
Where Next?

Upper School Academics & Curriculum
At Reigate Grammar School, the Upper School curriculum is designed not just to achieve excellent exam results, but to inspire a love of learning that lasts far beyond GCSEs.
We believe that with time, space and the right support, students can do more than simply succeed, they can flourish.
Our students begin GCSE study in the Third Form (Year 9), a year earlier than most schools. This allows them to explore subjects in greater depth and breadth, building confidence and reducing the pressure of a two-year sprint. It also gives more time for reflection, review and refinement of subject choices, ensuring that every student follows a bespoke path built around their interests, abilities and aspirations.
Stretch, curiosity and time to do it well
Upper School (Age 13-16)
Required Subjects
Most students take ten GCSEs, including:
In Maths, students are grouped by ability, with the most advanced students offered Further Maths as an additional qualification.
English Language
English Literature
Mathematics
Chemistry
Optional Classes
Students then select from a wide range of options in:
There is no one-size-fits-all approach — each student is guided by expert staff to build a programme that suits their goals, closely advised by the Careers Department.
View all the available GCSE Subjects
The Humanities
Languages
Technology
Social Sciences.
Empowering Students to Think, Create, and Lead
At RGS, we don’t just teach students what to learn — we teach them how to think. Through our membership of the international High Performance Learning programme, students develop powerful cognitive habits and learning behaviours. They learn how to analyse, create, connect and reflect, building intellectual confidence, creative problem-solving skills and the ability to thrive in a changing world.
This philosophy underpins every subject, and it empowers students to become truly future ready — able to meet academic challenges, but also to lead, adapt and grow with purpose and passion.
The Electives Programme
Our innovative Electives Programme is a key feature of the Upper School. These short, modular courses give students the opportunity to follow their interests, try something new, or develop practical life skills — all without the pressure of exams.
This rich variety keeps learning joyful and relevant, helping students feel engaged, confident, and excited about their journey.
Entrepreneurship or charity leadership
Photography, Film appreciation or animation
A New Language
Clay Modelling or Digital Creativity
Forensic Psychology, Global Politics, or Public Speaking
Informed and Future Ready
We help students become the architects of their own journey.
With PSHEE and weekly PE also part of the programme, students emerge from the Upper School not only with great results, but as well-rounded, informed and future ready individuals equipped for Sixth Form and beyond.

RGS Senior Schools
Families can choose between Reigate Grammar School and RGS Surrey Hills within the RGS Family.
Reigate Grammar School senior schools offer exceptional co-ed day schooling in Surrey – with boarding available and a shared focus on happiness, character and success.
Reigate Grammar School is one of the UK’s leading co-educational day schools, recently named the Top Co-Ed Day School in the South East 2026 (The Sunday Times, Parent Power) and The Sunday Times Independent School of the Year 2025. Located in Reigate, Surrey, RGS is known for its warm community, outstanding pastoral care and excellent academic outcomes.
From ages 11 to 18, students are supported to flourish as individuals, developing confidence, character and curiosity alongside exceptional results. With a vibrant co-curricular life, global partnerships, and a commitment to kindness and inclusion, RGS offers more than just education, it offers a foundation for life.
RGS Surrey Hills is a new senior school option within the RGS family and shares the same values and aspirations, currently enrolling for Year 7 in September 2026. Located near Dorking, it is a smaller, inclusive school where every teacher will know your child. It offers families access to the trusted RGS experience in a more personalised setting in 26 acres of countryside, and is part of the same charitable foundation and leadership as RGS, ensuring shared standards, ethos and opportunity.
Academically ambitious and delivered with RGS inspired teaching, learning and leadership, the personalised pathways and expert guidance enable every child to achieve excellent results and progress to leading universities. Unique, flexible and enabling curriculum pathways include a 3-year GCSE programme followed by the choice between both IB and A Levels - no other local school offers all of these avenues.
Both schools provide exceptional teaching in inspiring environments, supported by a culture where children are known and nurtured. Whether at Reigate Grammar School or RGS Surrey Hills near Dorking, families can expect an education that enables every child to thrive in and beyond the classroom - academically, emotionally and socially.
To learn more, visit one of our open events this term and discover the difference a Reigate Grammar School education can make.

Annual Open Day 2026
Find out what makes the RGS experience unique.
From outstanding academic results and exceptional pastoral care to friendships, fairgrounds, music, sport and icerinks, it all comes together to create a school where students truly thrive.
Our Annual Open Morning is the perfect opportunity for families to experience the energy and atmosphere of RGS. We encourage you to bring your child along for a fun and engaging morning, with interactive activities, exciting departmental experiences and plenty to discover.
Explore the school, visit every department and meet the staff and students who make our community so special. You will hear from the Headmaster, Mr Fenton, before touring the school with a student guide and gaining a real insight into the warmth, ambition and sense of belonging that define the RGS experience.
Headmaster’s Talks
There will be six Headmaster’s talks throughout the morning. Please book your preferred time slot.
Named The Sunday Times Independent School of the Year 2025, Education Today School of the Year 2024 and shortlisted for TES Independent Senior School of the Year 2025. Rated Excellent in all areas by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI), RGS is regularly featured among the UK’s top coeducational day schools in the Times and the Telegraph league tables.

Sixth Form (Years 12 & 13)
Fee Assistance & Bursaries
The RGS Fee Assistance Programme
Our enhanced Fee Assistance Programme brings together a number of initiatives to open the door to an RGS education for more families.
At Reigate Grammar School, we are committed to making our exceptional education accessible to talented children from all backgrounds. Our Fee Assistance Programme provides support to families who may need help with school fees, ensuring that financial circumstances never stand in the way of opportunity.
Whether you are applying for a full bursary or a small amount of support to help bridge the gap, our team is here to talk you through the process with warmth, care and complete confidentiality.
There are no limits to opportunity at RGS. We believe that every child deserves the chance to flourish.
Bursaries
Bursaries can offer up to 100% fee remission, plus help with uniform, meals, IT equipment and travel. These awards are means-tested, and based on both financial need and your child’s performance in our entrance assessments. Parents' income and assets will be reviewed annually in order to ensure that families continue to receive an appropriate level of support and all the information will be treated in the strictest confidence. The exact amount of fee reduction will depend upon family financial circumstances.
Bursaries provide vital financial assistance to individuals and families in need of support. Funding is drawn from both the School and the 1675 Bursary Fund, which invites the Reigatian Community to contribute to through our Changing Lives, Building Futures campaign. Through this initiative, we are able to offer transformational bursaries that create life-changing educational opportunities.
Reigate Grammar School
Any family with a gross annual income below £140,000 (higher if more than one child attends).
Throughout the child's time at RGS, but subject to annual review.
Please indicate your interest in a bursary when completing the online application form.
Who Can Apply?
Bursaries are available for children applying for 11+, 13+ and 16+ entry who demonstrate potential and would benefit from an RGS education. Awards are means-tested and based on an assessment of family income and assets.
While we do everything we can to help, bursary funds are limited, and not every eligible candidate can be offered a place. The earlier you register your interest, the more likely we will be able to help.
As a guideline, families with a total gross income above £140,000 are unlikely to qualify for bursary support, but please do get in touch to discuss your individual situation.
How to Apply
All information is treated in strict confidence, and we are always happy to talk things through with you personally.
Bursary application deadlines can be found in our Key Dates section for each entry point. Please ensure forms are submitted on time so we can consider your application.
Want to talk?
Choosing the right school for your child is a big decision, and we are here to support you at every step. Whether you are wondering if you might qualify for support, or just want to learn more about how bursaries work, our Admissions Team and Bursar are happy to help.
[email protected] 01737 222231

Scholarships
All RGS students flourish here, developing their talents and skills, and demonstrating high levels of performance both academically and in the wider curriculum.
Scholarships recognise those students with exceptional ability or potential in a specific area and seek to nurture this throughout their time at the school by delivering a programme of enrichment and mentoring.
Scholarships are available at 11+, 13+ and 16+ entry points, and reflect our belief in developing the whole child. From musicians and sportspeople to actors, artists and academic high-flyers, scholars are given additional support and opportunities to stretch their talents and lead by example within the wider school community.
Unlocking your full potential at RGS.
Types of Scholarships
Scholarship Awards & Support
The majority of scholarships either have no fee remission or are at a fixed amount (e.g. 5%). In exceptional circumstances a percentage reduction of fees may be given. Substantial fee reduction through scholarships is rare and is intended for candidates performing at an exceptionally high level, for example, national representative standard in the chosen sport. Scholarships may be held alongside bursaries where candidates qualify for additional fee support.
All scholars are mentored and supported throughout their time at RGS, helping them make the most of the opportunities available and grow in confidence and character.
How to Apply
To apply for a scholarship (excluding academic), simply indicate your interest when completing the RGS application form. You will then receive a separate scholarship application form closer to the exam date.
This form must include a reference from an independent referee (such as a music teacher, coach or drama tutor). Only applications that meet the criteria for each scholarship will be considered for assessment.
Academic scholarships are automatic and do not require a separate application.
If you have any questions or would like to speak to someone about which scholarship might be right for your child, our friendly Admissions Team is always happy to help: [email protected] 01737 222231

Trips, Visits & Expeditions
Expanding horizons, building memories, bringing learning to life.
At Reigate Grammar School, learning does not stop at the classroom door. Our extensive trips and expeditions programme offers students the chance to explore the world around them, deepen their academic understanding, build friendships and confidence, and create memories that last a lifetime.
Where Learning Meets Adventure
From Europe’s cultural capitals to South African sports tours, glacial landscapes in Iceland to community work in Croatia, RGS students are encouraged to broaden their perspectives and embrace adventure.
Our trips are designed to complement classroom learning and enrich school life. Some run every year, others as part of a two- or three-year cycle, ensuring all students will have the chance to take part during their time at RGS.
Belong (Student Life at RGS)
Co-Curricular
Academic Trips
Sports Tours
Outdoor Education & Leadership
Creative & Performance Trips
Learning Beyond the Classroom
These trips are an important part of what it means to be a Reigatian. They ignite curiosity, nurture independence, and reinforce our ethos of Be Happy, Belong, and Become Future Ready.
Students return from trips with wider perspectives, stronger friendships, and the self-belief to take on whatever comes next.
Education is more than lessons, at RGS it is about creating opportunities that inspire curiosity, build confidence, and spark lifelong passions. Through challenge, adventure, and shared experience, students discover who they are and what they can become.

Drama
At Reigate Grammar School, drama is for everyone.
Whether your child dreams of the spotlight or prefers to work behind the scenes, our thriving Drama Department offers a wealth of opportunities to explore, create and perform.
Drama is a powerful tool for building confidence, creativity, collaboration and critical thinking - skills that benefit students both in and out of the classroom. From the first lessons in Year 7 to performing on national stages, drama is a valued and celebrated part of life at RGS.
Belong (Student Life at RGS)
A Journey Through Drama at RGS
Co-Curricular Drama
Drama at RGS is dynamic and inclusive, with a packed programme of performances and events across the year. Recent productions include Shakespeare in Love, Treasure Island, Peter Pan and every year offers something new.
Co-curricular highlights include:
3–4 major productions each year
Studio performances and exam showcases
Monologue and choreography competitions
Masterclasses with industry professionals
Touring & Festivals
We are proud to take our work beyond the school grounds. The department has performed at:
National Student Drama Festival
Brighton Fringe Festival
Edinburgh Fringe Festival
These experiences offer ambitious students the chance to perform, direct and manage productions in professional, inspiring environments.
Facilities
The Drama Department is housed in two fully equipped black box studios and a third multi-purpose space with a recording studio, costume workshop and props store. Main school productions take place in the versatile Concert Hall, which can be adapted for both intimate performances and large-scale musicals, or at external venues such Leatherhead Theatre or The Ambassadors Theatre, London.
Scholarships and Opportunities
Drama scholarships are available at 11+, 13+ and 16+. Scholars are supported to develop their performance and leadership skills, with regular mentoring and access to additional opportunities.
Applying for a Scholarship? | More Information Here
Drama at RGS is about more than just performance. It is about building confidence, developing creative and technical skills, and feeling part of a community where everyone has a role to play, whether on stage, backstage, or in the audience.

Music
Music plays a central role in life at Reigate Grammar School, enriching daily school life, nurturing creativity and collaboration, and offering a space for students to thrive.
Whether your child is an experienced musician or just beginning their journey, they will find a welcoming and vibrant community here.
We are proud of our strong musical tradition and the inclusive approach that sits at its heart. From orchestras and rock bands to choirs, swing groups and chamber ensembles, there is something for every musical interest and ability. Music at RGS is about enjoyment, growth and expression, and we actively encourage students to explore their potential in a supportive and stimulating environment.
Belong (Student Life at RGS)
Growing Through Music
Music and Academic Success
Some of our highest-achieving academic students are also among our most committed musicians. Music provides more than just creative fulfilment, it cultivates essential skills such as communication, discipline, organisation and emotional intelligence. That’s why we champion balance: not only does it lead to happier students, it often leads to better outcomes.
We actively encourage variety in our young people’s lives in order to maintain a healthy balance – but also because it helps to produce better results.
— Headmaster Shaun Fenton
Co-Curricular Music
Students are encouraged to take part in one or more of the many ensembles on offer. Performing with others builds confidence and camaraderie, and above all, it’s fun.
These groups perform at regular concerts throughout the year, both in school and in the wider community. Students also contribute to assemblies and special events – music is woven into the rhythm of everyday life at RGS.
Orchestra and string ensemble
Concert bands and swing band
Six choirs
Guitar, percussion, wind and brass ensembles
Chamber groups and rock bands
Individual Tuition
In addition to classroom music, we offer individual tuition in a wide range of instruments and voice. Lessons are timetabled to minimise disruption to academic work and are available for any student who wishes to learn.
The RGS Saturday Music College
Open to young musicians from across the region, the RGS Saturday Music College offers a wide-reaching programme for 7-18 year olds. With individual lessons, chamber music, composition and musicianship classes – plus regular concerts and expert masterclasses – it’s a dynamic and welcoming place for students to grow their talents.
Scholarships and Choral Awards
Music scholarships are available at 11+, 13+ and 16+ entry points. These awards are designed to support and nurture talented musicians, offering additional opportunities to perform and develop.
We also offer choral awards through the RGS Godfrey Searle Choir, a special opportunity for exceptional young singers aged 7-15. Choristers rehearse and perform regularly, enjoying cathedral tours and prestigious events, from services at St Paul’s Cathedral to international performances. They receive outstanding vocal training and become part of a unique musical tradition at RGS.
Applying for a Scholarship? | More Information Here
Music at RGS continues to thrive, and I am always humbled by the way it brings people together.Whether through grand events or the many rehearsals, concerts, and musical moments that fill our school year, the passion and commitment of our students never fail to inspire.

Governors
Our Board of Governors helps to guide and support Reigate Grammar School, bringing experience and insight from a range of backgrounds.
The Chair of Governors can be contacted through the Clerk to the Governors, Mrs Helena Briggs by email [email protected] or via the main Reigate Grammar School telephone number 01737 222231.
RGS Community
Mr Mark Elsey - Chair
Educated at Reigate Grammar School and King’s College London, Mr Elsey is a senior consultant at the international law firm Ashurst LP, having recently stepped down after 30 years as a partner. He specialises in the development and financing of large scale infrastructure projects and headed Ashurst's global Energy and Infrastructure department for 12 years.
Mr Elsey’s family connections with the school are extensive: Mr Elsey met his wife, Mrs Jacqueline Elsey, while at RGS; his father and father-in-law both attended the school as did his son and daughter.
Mr Elsey is a member of Old Reigatian RFC and of Tandridge and Betchworth Golf Clubs.
Mark joined the Board of Governors of Reigate Grammar School in 2012 and was appointed Chair at the end of 2021.
Mr Duncan Anderson
Duncan was a Micklefield Governor from 2018 and joined the RGS Board in 2024 when the schools merged. He is a member of the Finance & Foundation Committee.
Duncan was educated at Hereford Cathedral School before graduating in mathematics from Cambridge University and then qualifying as a Fellow of the Institute of Actuaries.
He has worked for WTW and its predecessor companies (Watsons, Watson Wyatt, EMB, Towers Watson) for over 35 years, in both general insurance consultancy and related software development. He specialises in motor insurance pricing analytics and has spoken on this in seminars in over 30 countries. Since 2017 he has led WTW’s global Insurance Technology business, which provides specialist software to over 1,000 insurers worldwide.
Duncan is married with four daughters, all of whom attended RGS. He has been a resident of Reigate since 1990.
Dr Shrilla Banerjee
Shrilla joined the Board of Governors in 2021 and is a member of the Education & Welfare Committee.
Shrilla is a Consultant Cardiologist with a specialist interest in prevention and intervention (angioplasty and stenting) of coronary artery disease. Her research interests lie in Women’s Cardiovascular Health and she was also a Cardiologist for the Civil Aviation Authority assessing fitness to fly of commercial and private pilot licence holders.
In her current position at East Surrey Hospital, Dr Banerjee is the Lead for Education, responsible for the training and supervision of cardiology trainees, and runs the cardiology Education programme. She is also an NHS Ambassador for Education, involved in the work experience programme for schools.
She was elected on to the Council of the British Cardiovascular Society and the British Cardiovascular Intervention Society, where she Chaired the Focus Group for Women in Interventional Cardiology looking at how we can attract more women into Interventional Cardiology, support existing female trainees and Consultants and ensure excellent representation and visibility of women in the field.
Outside of work, Shrilla enjoys spending time with her family, keeping fit and painting.
Mr Marc Benton
Marc is the Chair of the Finance & Foundation Committee and has been Governor on the RGS Board since 2015.
Marc has worked for the North Sea Transition Authority (the “NSTA”) since 2020 as the Head of Investor Finance. The NSTA is part of the UK Government charged with regulating the UK offshore oil and gas industry and developing the energy transition. Prior to this role, Marc was an experienced Managing Director with a successful 23 year history of working in the investment banking industry. Skilled in M&A and general corporate advisory, Capital Markets funding (equity and debt/high yield) and general Corporate Finance for Corporates, NOCs and Private Equity. He led regional investment banking sector teams for 12 years in both EMEA and APAC. He has a Bachelor of Commerce (BCom) with French from the University of Birmingham and a European Master of Business Science from Ecole Superieure de Commerce, Clermont Ferrand, France.
Mrs Helen Crossley
A former St Christopher’s Governor, Helen joined the RGS Board of Governors following the merger with St Christopher’s in May 2025. She sits on the Education and Welfare Committee.
Helen became a governor of St Christopher’s in 2012 following her retirement as Head of the prep School at Ewell Castle, having previously held the post of Deputy Head of the Junior School at City of London Freemen’s School. She was Chair of Governors at St Christopher’s from November 2016 to June 2021.
Helen is delighted to be able to use the experience she has gained throughout her career in a strategic role within the RGS Group of Schools with a particular focus on the prep and pre-prep age groups.
Mrs Mary Edmunds
Mary joined the Board of Governors of Reigate Grammar School in 2018 with a focus on strategy, people and growth.
Mary sits on the board for Hines Europe Limited, a global commercial real estate firm. Educated in the US with global experience in business transformation, human resources and strategy, Mrs Edmunds arrived at Reigate Grammar School with a global perspective. Mrs Edmunds is a Senior Managing Director for Hines Real Estate. She studied Economics and Psychology at Vanderbilt University in the United States and her Masters of Business at Exeter University, UK.
Mrs. Edmunds has worked in business education with Harvard University since 2014 to deliver leadership programmes for a sovereign wealth fund in the Middle East. Having seen education from a global perspective and taking a deep interest in the future of Reigate Grammar School,
Mary is married with two daughters, who both have graduated from Reigate Grammar School.
Mrs Joosje Hamilton
Joosje was appointed a governor at RGS in June 2024 following the merger with Micklefield – before that she was Chair of Governors at Micklefield School since December 2017. Joosje is a member of the Education & Welfare Committee.
She is a solicitor specialising in EU and UK competition and regulatory law and sits on the Education & Staffing Committee. A few years ago, she decided to leave full-time employment in the City and became a part-time legal consultant. She now spends the majority of her time running and developing her family’s agricultural estate, including managing its residential and commercial property portfolio. Joosje’s three daughters had a wonderful education and happy time at Micklefield School and RGS and she is therefore delighted to contribute to the future success of the RGS Group of Schools.
Mrs Maxine Hulme
Maxine is Vice Chair of the RGS Board and Chair of the Governance and Risk Committee. She joined the RGS Board following the partnership between RGS and Chinthurst School, announced in March 2017. She was previously the Chair of Governors at Chinthurst School.
Maxine has been working in the private sector since 2016 within financial services where she has worked in financial services transformation and is currently an operations Director.
In her earlier career, Maxine served as Deputy Assistant Commissioner in the Metropolitan Police Service, holding senior roles in Transformation, Operations and Intelligence. In recognition of outstanding service, she was awarded the Queen’s Policing Medal in 2014.
Mrs Lisa Page
Lisa joined the RGS board after the partnership between RGS and Chinthurst was announced in March 2017. She was appointed Chair of Education and Welfare for the RGS group in March 2025.
She is an accomplished Healthcare Director with a career in operational management within the UK's Healthcare sector with a strong track record in growing private patient healthcare services within NHS trusts, within some of the world's leading hospitals in London.
Throughout her career Lisa has held a range of senior leadership roles with operational oversight, strategic planning and complex capital projects across multiple sites. She is passionate about service excellence and consistently delivering outstanding outcomes, which has been recognised through multiple awards for best hospital performance.
Lisa has extensive international travel experience to expand services abroad whilst establishing and strengthening strategic global partnerships.
Mr Dominic Roberts
Dominic joined the RGS Board of Governors in May 2025 following the merger with St Christopher’s and is on the Finance and Foundation committee. He was previously the Chair at St Christopher’s School.
After studying Physics at Bristol University Dominic became a Chartered Accountant and, upon becoming a partner in 2005, specialising in providing advice to Companies looking to IPO or already listed on the London stock markets. Since 2019 he has been the managing partner of PKF in London, Leeds and Manchester, responsible for setting and overseeing the strategic and operational direction of the business and its people. He is also Chair of the EMEI region of the PKF Global Accounting Network and a Global Board member.
Dominic is the father of two girls who attended St Christopher’s and continue to cherish the friends and memories from their years at the school many years later.
Mrs Maggie Stilwell
Maggie joined the Board in 2023 and is a member of the Finance & Foundation Committee.
Maggie has recently retired as a Partner at EY, having worked for the firm for 28 years specialising in forensic accountancy. Maggie has worked across industries for clients during that time, as well as having a senior management position for the firm of EY. Maggie has given evidence to courts and arbitrations on behalf of her clients, and acted as judge for commercial disputes requiring an expert determination process. Prior to working at EY, Maggie worked at PwC in the audit practice, qualifying as a Chartered Accountant. She holds a First Class Honours degree in Business from Edinburgh University.
Mrs Rebecca Sturt
Rebecca joined the board following the merger with Micklefield in 2024 and is a member of the Education & Welfare Committee.
Rebecca graduated from Cambridge University with a master’s in manufacturing engineering. She worked in the energy sector and medical equipment manufacturing before becoming a teacher in 2004. She has worked in education for 20 years as a maths teacher and more recently has also been an EPQ coordinator.
Mr Chris Townsend
Chris was a Governor on the Board at Boxhill School previously and joined the RGS Board following the merger in 2025. Chris is a member of the Education & Welfare committee and oversees the Boarding at RGS Surrey Hills.
Chris has been the Head at Felsted School in Essex for the last decade, having previously worked at Stowe and Dean Close. He taught Classics and has also held roles as Deputy Head, Head of Boarding and Master in charge of Cricket and was a Housemaster of both day and boarding houses. In April 2026, he will take up the Headship at Cheltenham College. Chris is also on the Board at Essex Cricket club and is a trustee of the charity Chance to Shine, as well as being an ISI Inspector.
Mr Nick Weber
Nick joined the Board of Governors of Reigate Grammar School in 2018 and is a member of the Finance & Foundation Committee.
He holds a degree in Chemical Engineering from Princeton University. All five of his children have been educated at Reigate Grammar School.
Nick is the Founder and CEO of Henderson Park, a 92 person real estate investment firm focused on the UK and Continental Europe. Henderson Park manages $6 billion of investor equity, and to date has invested over $14 billion in building a portfolio of real estate assets across Europe.
Prior to founding Henderson Park, Nick was a founding partner at Mount Kellett, an $8 billion multi-asset class investment platform, and ran its European operations from 2008 to 2015. Before joining Mount Kellett, Nick spent 15 years at Goldman Sachs, becoming a partner in 2006.
Mr Ed Wheeler
Ed is the Chair of the Estates & Premises Committee and joined the RGS Board in 2021.
Educated at Douai School, Reading and the Polytechnic of the South Bank, Ed qualified as a Chartered Quantity Surveyor in 1986, becoming a Fellow of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors in 1994. He joined his firm as a Director in 1987 and has been Chairman since 1997.
His practice encompasses all aspects of construction cost and contract consultancy and has successfully delivered a wide range of commissions for major national and international Clients as well as UK developers, public authorities, charities and private clients often working closely with world renowned design teams.
Ed is a member of Old Reigatian RFC and the MCC and is married with two sons, both of whom attended RSM and RGS.

Sixth Form (Years 12 & 13)
Leadership & Enrichment
There is always something going on – something to plan, something to lead, something to make better.
Sixth Formers don’t just take part – they help shape the whole school.
Leadership and enrichment are at the heart of Sixth Form life at Reigate Grammar School. Whether it is running a club, leading a committee, launching a legacy project or mentoring younger students, RGS Sixth Formers are given the freedom and responsibility to make their mark.
Every Sixth Former is encouraged to take on a role, contribute to the community, and grow in confidence, initiative and independence. Leadership at RGS is about action, creativity and contribution. It’s about stepping forward and making a difference.
Growing Leaders, Building Legacies
Sixth Form (Ages 16 to 18)
Committees and Leadership for All
In Lower Sixth, every student takes on a leadership role within one of our core committees. These include:
Each committee meets weekly to plan events, shape school culture and develop initiatives. Students receive weekly leadership training delivered by the Sixth Form team, covering topics such as communication, teamwork, organisation, and strategic planning.
Academic
EDI (Equality, Diversity & Inclusion)
Wellbeing
Music
Global Village
E-Sports
RGS Future Leaders Programme
Students can also opt into the RGS Future Leaders course, an additional enrichment programme for those who want to take their leadership journey further. It includes:
In 2024, over 30 students graduated from this programme.
Real-world project work
Networking with industry leaders
Head Students & Prefects
Our Senior Prefect team and Heads of School are appointed based on their committee contributions and leadership throughout the year. These students also receive external training with leadership specialists and help mentor younger students in the Upper School Leadership Diploma.
Leadership here is earned, supported and celebrated and its impact is felt across the school.
Enrichment Through Action
RGS Sixth Form life is bursting with co-curricular opportunities, many of them student-led:
From Philosophy to Film Production
One of the largest Model United Nations
Events in the South East, run by Sixth Formers
Like Earthshot, E-Sports, and Medical Discussion Group
In large-scale music and drama productions
Outstanding Sport and performing Arts provision
With students regularly achieving County, Regional and Even National Honours
A thriving Combined Cadet Force
Developing Leadership, Resilience and Teamwork
The largest Duke of Edinburgh’s
Award Scheme programme in the country with Bronze, Silver and Gold expeditions every year
On School-Wide Outreach, Wellbeing, Fundraising and House Events
Whether you want to lead, create, organise or inspire, there is room for every voice and we will help you develop the skills to lead with purpose and confidence.
Trips, Talks & Experiences
Our Sixth Formers broaden their horizons through local, national and international opportunities, including:
Leadership visits and conferences
Specialist career networking events, often student-led
It’s also about fun!
From the Winter Formal to the Leavers’ Day Fairground, Sixth Form life includes celebration, friendship and fun. There are:
We believe enrichment should be as much about fun, belonging and shared memories as it is about skills and CVs.
Regular informal socials and café events
Sixth Form–only trips
The Winter Formal and the Leavers’ Ball
Ready to lead?
We believe that the Student leadership programme helps to bridge the gap between school and professional life, providing our students with the tools they need to succeed in later life.

GCSE Results
At Reigate Grammar School, we are proud of a long tradition of great academic results.
Consistent success. Outstanding standards.
Our students consistently perform at the highest levels, and our results reflect not only academic ability, but a culture of support and ambition in learning.
RGS results year after year prove that happy students, excellent teaching, and personalised support make a winning combination.
